# Heros Agents

**https://heros-agent.space** — seven agents that do real work and say plainly what they did not,
plus **Market watch**: what could move the US stock market over the next two weeks, and which way.
The whole site is in English and 中文.

## The agents

| Agent | What it does | Where |
|---|---|---|
| **Heros** | Evaluates an AI agent: point her at a repository, she assesses it across nine axes, and opens a pull request only once you say yes | https://eval.heros-agent.space |
| **阿桥 Opportunity Bridge** | Finds real jobs, training and subsidies, and reads the public conditions out to you one by one; never decides eligibility for you | https://jobs.heros-agent.space |
| **FORGE** | Engineering design out loud: describe a part, get a shape you can rotate, section and measure, with the reasoning behind every decision | https://forge.heros-agent.space |
| **Vera · 维拉** | Prepares legal cases and looks after your health; licensed attorneys and physicians sign off on everything that matters | https://act.heros-agent.space |
| **Aoi · 葵** | Game night: Texas Hold’em with friends and AI players, and board games designed from your description; play money only | https://play.heros-agent.space |
| **Suki** | Dating: introduces you to people in your city, coaches the conversation and plans the date; a match takes two yeses. Mobile app, not in the stores yet | https://match.heros-agent.space |
| **鸭鸭 · 转租鸭 Sublet Duck** | Sublets: compares walking away with subletting when you leave a lease early, drafts the listing from one sentence, helps seekers compare and spot scams; publishing, contact details and viewings wait for your tap. WeChat mini program | https://zhuanzuya.zhiyuwujie.top |

They share three habits: **ask before guessing**, **a person signs off** on anything that costs money or
can’t be undone, and **keep the record** of who asked, what ran and what changed.

## Market watch

At **https://heros-agent.space/markets/**.

**The question it answers:** *what is scheduled over the next two weeks that could move the Dow Jones,
the Nasdaq Composite and the S&P 500, and which way is each index more likely to go?*

### What you see

| Part | What it shows |
|---|---|
| **Index strip** | The last close and daily change for the Dow, Nasdaq and S&P 500, plus the VIX and the 10-year Treasury yield |
| **Timeline** | Every trading day in the next two weeks, in order. Before the open, today's call shows the overnight futures it was read from. Each day opens with a **session call** for each index. Under it are the day’s events, each with its time (Eastern), category, impact level, consensus and prior figures, and an **up ▲ or down ▼ call for each index, with a probability and how big the reaction is likely to be** |
| **Calendar** | Monday-to-Friday weeks. Each day shows how many events it has, how many are high impact, and the three session calls. Pick a day to see its events. Past days show what the index actually did, with ✓ or ✗ against the call |
| **Track record** | How often the calls were right for each index, how often the calls with a lean were right, and a Brier score (0.25 is a coin flip; lower is better) |
| **The pre-open signal, tested** | How often the close followed the opening move on the last 12 months of sessions the model never saw, next to simply leaning up, and how the 9:20 AM futures reading did over the last ~50 sessions |
| **Event details** | A one-line read of the event, the upside and downside cases, what to watch, how confident the call is, and where the data came from |
| **How this was made** | When it was last updated, how many sources answered, whether any analysis was sent back and redone, and whether the calls came from the AI analyst or the rules-based baseline |
| **Headlines** | The latest market-moving headlines |

You can filter to **Fed & macro**, **earnings** or **high impact only**. The page remembers your view and
language, and works on a phone.

### What it covers

| Category | Events |
|---|---|
| **Fed** | FOMC rate decisions (including the meetings with the dot plot), minutes, the Fed Chair’s speeches |
| **Inflation** | CPI, PCE, PPI |
| **Jobs** | The monthly jobs report (payrolls, unemployment, wages), JOLTS job openings, ADP, weekly jobless claims |
| **Growth & consumer** | GDP, ISM manufacturing and services, retail sales, consumer confidence and sentiment, durable goods, housing |
| **Earnings** | Companies worth $200 billion or more, marked when they are in the Dow or are Nasdaq heavyweights |

High-impact events (FOMC, CPI, PCE, the jobs report, GDP, the largest companies’ earnings) usually move
all three indices. Low-impact ones rarely move any. The timeline lists the most important first, up to
36 events.

Data comes from the Federal Reserve, Nasdaq’s economic and earnings calendars, Yahoo Finance for index
levels, and CNBC and MarketWatch for headlines.

### How a call is made

1. **A baseline** starts from what it can show: the market’s long-run tendency to rise, the past week’s
   momentum, what consensus expects compared with last time, and for earnings, expected growth. Once a
   figure is released, the **surprise versus consensus** takes over. A hot inflation print usually hurts
   stocks, the Nasdaq most; strong growth usually helps, the Dow most.
2. **The AI analyst** reads the events, the market’s levels and the headlines, sees the baseline, and
   makes its own call for each index: up or down, a probability, and the likely size of the move, with
   a short explanation in both languages. If it disagrees with the baseline, it says why.
3. **An independent critic** checks every analysis. It sends one back if it cites a number that isn’t
   in the data, sounds like investment advice, or is more certain than the evidence allows. A rejected
   analysis is redone once. If it still fails, the page shows the baseline call and says so.
4. **The session call** for each day combines that day’s events, weighted by how much each index is
   exposed to each one. A quiet day leans on the market’s longer-run tendency.
5. **Every call is scored.** A day’s call is locked before the 9:30 AM ET open and can’t be changed
   afterwards. After the close it is checked against what the index actually did, and the result goes
   into the track record.

### The pre-open call: where the real edge is

For a day a week away, nobody knows which way the market will close, so those calls stay close to
50%. The one strong, measurable guide is **where the market opens**. Over the last five years, when the
S&P 500 opened more than 0.5% higher it closed higher 84% of the time; when it opened more than 0.5%
lower it closed higher only 13% of the time. Index futures trade overnight and show where the open is
heading.

So on every trading day:

1. At **9:20 AM ET** the desk reads S&P 500, Nasdaq-100 and Dow futures against the previous 4 PM ET close.
2. It turns that move into a probability with a model fitted on five years of history, and combines it
   with the day's events.
3. At **9:30 AM ET**, the open, the call **locks**. Later updates can't change it; the page marks it
   "Locked at the open" and scores it against the close.

Tested on the last 12 months of sessions the model never saw, this was right about **70% of the time**
(Dow 69%, S&P 500 70%, Nasdaq 73%) against 53% for leaning up every day. Read from futures at 9:20, as it
is done live, it was right 69–81% of the time over the last 48 sessions. The model is refitted every
Sunday, and an independent check refuses it unless it beats leaning up on data it hasn't seen.

**After-hours reports:** when a company such as Microsoft or Amazon reports after the close, its stock
moves in after-hours trading. The desk translates that move into each index — by company size for the
S&P 500 and Nasdaq, by share price for the Dow — and folds it into the next morning's call.

**No clear lean:** a call between 48% and 52% shows as "– No clear lean" instead of an arrow. It still
counts in the Brier score, but the track record also shows how the calls with a lean did on their own.

### How sure it is

Days ahead, the probabilities stay modest: at most 66% from the baseline and 85% from the AI analyst,
and most sit close to 50–60%, because honestly that is how much anyone can know in advance. The
pre-open call can go higher — up to 90% — when futures have moved clearly. The track record is there
so you can judge the calls for yourself.

### When it updates

Three times each weekday, at **7:30 AM, 12:00 PM and 4:30 PM Eastern**, plus the **9:20 AM pre-open
update**, and again **15 minutes after each major release**, so the timeline shows the actual figure (or
the after-hours reaction) and a fresh call.

### What it is not

Market watch is AI-generated market commentary, for information only. It is **not investment advice**:
no buy or sell recommendations, no price targets, no single-stock picks. Market holidays are not shown
as closed yet.

# Running and deploying heros-agent.space

The landing page and the Market watch page (`site/markets/`) are static HTML/CSS (English / 中文 toggle),
served by unprivileged nginx. Market watch reads `/data/market/timeline.json`, which the market desk in [`market/`](../market/README.md)
publishes.

## Run locally

```bash
python -m http.server 8088 -d site                 # the page
cd market && python -m desk run                    # one refresh → site/data/market/timeline.json
```

## Deploy

A k3s node reached over SSM, with Traefik and cert-manager (`letsencrypt-prod`). Both releases need the
AWS CLI signed in to the account that owns the node, Docker with `buildx`, and a clean, committed tree.

The node's instance id is not in this repository. Put it in `deploy/deploy.env`, which is gitignored:

```bash
cp deploy/deploy.env.example deploy/deploy.env   # then set INSTANCE
```

| What | Namespace | Command |
|---|---|---|
| Landing page | `home`: no database, no secrets, no egress | `deploy/release.sh` (build arm64 → ECR `heros-home` → apply by digest) |
| Market desk | `market`: PostgreSQL, coordinator, workers, read-only web | `market/deploy/release.sh` (build arm64 → ECR `heros-market` → apply by digest) |

Both take `--dry-run` for a server-side dry run. Deploy the desk first, so `/data/market/timeline.json`
exists when the new page goes out. Until then the page shows a "not published yet" note.

## Images

Portraits in `site/img/` are copied from each agent's own repository; update them there first.
Images are cached for 7 days: a changed image gets a new filename (`aqiao-2.webp` → `aqiao-3.webp`), never an overwrite.

# Market desk

The multi-agent system behind the **Market watch** page (`/markets/`): upcoming market-moving events with an
up/down call and a probability for the Dow, Nasdaq and S&P 500, each call scored against the close.
Python 3.11+. The standard library is enough locally (SQLite); PostgreSQL needs `psycopg[binary]`.
Product overview: [the repository README](../README.md#market-watch). Design: [DESIGN.md](DESIGN.md).

## Run locally

```bash
cd market
python -m desk run                 # one refresh: coordinator + 4 worker threads; writes ../site/data/market/timeline.json
python -m http.server 8088 -d ../site
```

The analyst calls `qwen3.7-plus` through the Qwen Token Plan's OpenAI-compatible API (a reasoning model:
about 200 s and ~75K tokens per refresh). It reads `QWEN_LLM_API_KEY_V2` from
the environment, or from the dotenv file named by `DESK_ENV_FILE` (default: `../../.ENV`, i.e.
`E:\repos\.ENV`). Without a working key it uses the rules baseline and says so on the page.

| Variable | Default |
|---|---|
| `DESK_LLM_BASE_URL` | `https://token-plan.maas.qianwenaiapi.com/compatible-mode/v1` |
| `DESK_LLM_MODEL` | `qwen3.7-plus` (the plan also lists `qwen3.7-max`, `qwen3.6-flash`, `deepseek-v4-pro`) |
| `DESK_LLM_USD_IN` / `DESK_LLM_USD_OUT` | `0` (prepaid plan; set per-1M-token prices for a metered endpoint) |
| `DESK_WINDOW_DAYS` | `14` |
| `DESK_DB` | `market/var/desk.sqlite3`, or a PostgreSQL DSN `postgresql://user:pass@host:5432/db` |
| `DESK_PUBLISH_DIR` | `site/data/market` |

## Run as services

```bash
python -m desk coordinator         # schedule, wake-ups, planning; one instance
python -m desk worker              # as many as you like; --roles analyst,critic to specialise
```

## Operate

```bash
python -m desk status              # recent missions
python -m desk explain <mission>   # what each agent did, why, and what happens next
python -m desk metrics             # completion, success, recovery, retries, cost, human interventions
python -m desk escalations
python -m desk approve <mission>   # release a publish that verification held back
python -m desk resolve <id> --action retry|skip|accept
python -m desk intents             # intents, agents, tools
```

## Database

All durable state lives in one database: missions, the task graph and its queue, the event log,
artifacts, checkpoints, idempotency records, locks, escalations, timers, long-term knowledge and usage.

| Where | Backend |
|---|---|
| local runs and tests | a SQLite file (WAL) |
| k8s (`market` namespace) | **PostgreSQL 16** (`desk-pg` StatefulSet, 2 Gi node-local volume) |

Both run the same SQL. On Postgres every write transaction takes one advisory lock, which serialises
writers the way SQLite's `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` does, so a task can never be claimed twice. The schema is
created on first start. Its password is generated on the node at first deploy and never leaves it.

To try Postgres locally:

```bash
docker run -d --name desk-pg -e POSTGRES_DB=desk -e POSTGRES_USER=desk -e POSTGRES_PASSWORD=change-me   -p 127.0.0.1:55432:5432 postgres:16-alpine
DESK_DB=postgresql://desk:change-me@127.0.0.1:55432/desk python -m desk run
```

## Evaluate

```bash
cd market && python -m unittest -v                                   # on SQLite
DESK_TEST_PG=postgresql://desk:change-me@127.0.0.1:55432/desk   python -m unittest -v                                              # the same 27 cases on Postgres
```

27 cases, no network: recorded source shapes, a fake clock and a fake model. With `DESK_TEST_PG`
every test starts from empty tables in that database, so point it at a throwaway one.

## Deploy

```bash
market/deploy/release.sh            # build arm64 → ECR heros-market → apply market/deploy/k8s/market.yaml by digest
market/deploy/release.sh --dry-run  # server-side dry run
```

It uses `INSTANCE` from `deploy/deploy.env` and `deploy/ssm.sh`, like the landing page's release. It needs
the AWS CLI signed in, Docker with `buildx`, and a clean, committed tree (the image is tagged with HEAD).

| In `market` | What |
|---|---|
| `desk-pg` | PostgreSQL 16; only the coordinator and workers can reach it |
| `desk-coordinator` | 1 replica: schedule, wake-ups, planning; waits for the database on start |
| `desk-worker` | 2 replicas, scale freely; the only pods with outbound HTTPS |
| `desk-web` | nginx serving `timeline.json` read-only at `heros-agent.space/data/market/` |

Secrets follow the node's convention for every agent (act, forge, play): one AWS Secrets Manager
secret, `market/prod`, read by the node's IAM role through External Secrets into the k8s secret `desk`.

| Property | What |
|---|---|
| `db-password` | generated by the release script the first time, kept after that; the DSN is built from it in-cluster |
| `llm-api-key` | `QWEN_LLM_API_KEY_V2`, copied from `../.ENV` on each release when it changed. If it's empty, the analyst uses the baseline |

The script also keeps a `MarketSecretsRead` inline policy on the node role, scoped to `market/*`.
Secret values pass through 0600 temp files only, never through arguments, output or the SSM command.

After rollout the script starts one refresh, so the page has data without waiting for the next slot.

# Market desk — design

The **Market watch** page (`/markets/`) shows the coming two weeks of market-moving events for the
Dow Jones (DJI), Nasdaq Composite (IXIC) and S&P 500 (GSPC). Each event gets an **up/down call per
index, with a probability**, and each trading day gets a combined session call. Calls are frozen at
the open and **scored against the close**, so the page shows its own track record.

It is not a group of LLMs talking to each other. It is a durable execution system: specialised
agents are stateless workers that lease tasks from a queue and act on shared, persistent state.

```
User goal / timer / event wake-up
  ↓
Mission Planner (intents.py)           intent → first layer of the task DAG
  ↓
Task graph + durable queue (queue.py)  DAG, leases, retries, backoff, approval gates
  ↓
Coordinator (coordinator.py)           plan → assign → observe → verify → update → replan
  ↓
Workers (worker.py) running agents (agents.py)
   researcher · news_scout · data · analyst · critic · verifier · publisher
  ↓
Tools (tools.py)                       permissioned, host-allowlisted, recorded
  ↓
Verification (critic + verifier)       independent of the agent that did the work
  ↓
Persistent state + artifacts (store.py: PostgreSQL in k8s, a SQLite file locally)
  ↓
Replan / continue / complete; publish; schedule wake-ups
```

## 1. Objective

| | |
|---|---|
| Business goal | Readers see which scheduled events could move the three indices, which way, and how sure the desk is |
| Success | `timeline.json` published; every event and every session in the window has three calls (direction, probability, magnitude); critic and verifier passed; past calls scored |
| Expected duration | 30 s – 3 min per refresh; three scheduled refreshes per weekday, plus one 15 min after each tier-1/2 release |
| Acceptable failures | any single source may fail (the timeline publishes without it); no model key → transparent rules baseline; more than half of the sources down → publish waits for a human; no events at all → no publish, escalate |

## 2. Intents

### Mission intents (become a task graph)

| Intent | Trigger | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `refresh_timeline` | timers 07:30 / 12:00 / 16:30 ET on weekdays; post-event wake-ups; `desk run` | collect → merge → verify → analyse ×N → critique ×N → assemble → verify → publish |
| `source_probe` | hourly timer; operator | one call per source; health stored in shared knowledge; three failures in a row escalate |
| `calibrate_signals` | Sundays 18:00 ET; first start with no calibration | 5-year daily history ×3 + 60-day 5-min futures ×3 → backtest (fit on 4 years, test on the last 252 sessions, check the 9:20 futures reading) → verifier (positive slope, ≥200 test sessions, beats the always-up baseline's Brier) → commit to `knowledge/calibration` |
| `preopen_call` | weekdays 09:20 ET | live futures ×3 → re-read today's call from the last published timeline → verify → publish; the 9:30 open locks it |

### Event-driven variants of `refresh_timeline`

| Variant | How it arises |
|---|---|
| post-release re-assessment | after publishing, the coordinator schedules a wake-up 15 min after every tier-1/2 release; the next run sees the *actual* figure and the surprise drives a stronger call |
| re-analysis with feedback | the critic rejects part of a batch → the coordinator adds `analyze.bN.r1` + `critic.bN.r1` for only those events, with the critic's feedback |

### Operator intents (the human surface, `python -m desk …`)

| Intent | Command |
|---|---|
| approve a held publish | `approve <mission>` |
| resolve an escalation (retry / skip / accept) | `resolve <id> --action …` |
| explain a run: who did what, why, what changed, what is next | `explain <mission>` |
| system reliability | `metrics` |
| mission and task status | `status [mission]` |
| cancel a mission | `cancel <mission>` |
| list the catalogue | `intents` |

### Reader intents (served by the page, no agent runs)

see the next two weeks as a timeline · see the same as a calendar · filter Fed & macro / earnings / high impact ·
open one day · read scenarios and the critic's review · check the track record · switch English / 中文.

### Intents deliberately not supported

Personalised investment advice, trade execution, price targets, single-stock picks. The analyst prompt
forbids advice language and the critic rejects it (`skills.ADVICE`); the page carries a disclaimer.

## 3. Agents (roles) and their contracts

Every agent gets **only** its task inputs and its dependencies' artifacts (local context), and only
the tools its contract grants. The mission state is global and only the coordinator reads it whole.

| Role | Ops | Permissions → tools | Reads | Writes | Limits | Escalates when |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Planner** (in the coordinator) | plan, replan | — | the intent and results | task specs | `max_tasks` 80, `max_depth` 3 | the graph is refused (cycle, budget) |
| **Coordinator** | assign, observe, replan, finish | state | everything | task / mission transitions, timers | deadline 20 min | a required task dies; deadline passes |
| **Researcher** | `fomc`, `macro`, `earnings` | net.read → `fomc_calendar`, `econ_calendar`, `earnings_calendar` | a date range or one day | events / raw rows | 60 s, 4 tool calls | never: optional, the mission degrades |
| **News scout** | `headlines` | net.read → `rss_headlines` | the feed list | de-duplicated headlines, market-relevance flag | 60 s, 5 calls | every feed fails |
| **Data** | `snapshot`, `merge`, `assemble` | net.read, state.read → `index_quote` | dependency artifacts | snapshot with 1-month history · ranked events · timeline with day outlooks, past results, track record | 90 s, 8 calls | no quotes; no events |
| **Analyst** | `analyze` | llm.call → `llm_json` | one batch of events + snapshot + headlines + the baseline call (+ critic feedback) | one call per index per event | 180 s, 2 calls; mission LLM budget | model unavailable → baseline; budget spent → baseline |
| **Critic** | `review` | none | the batch and the analyst's artifact | verdict per event + feedback | 30 s | never itself; the coordinator replans on its verdict |
| **Verifier** | `events`, `timeline` | none | the merge / assemble artifact | pass + risk flags, or a hard failure | 30 s | any invariant fails → no publish |
| **Publisher** (execution) | `publish` | fs.publish, state.read → `publish_file` | the verified timeline | the file, once per content; frozen session calls | 30 s, 1 call | risk flags → waits for a human |

## 4. Tools

| Tool | Permission | Side effect | Source | Guard |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `fomc_calendar(year)` | net.read | no | federalreserve.gov | layout-change detection → non-retryable |
| `econ_calendar(day)` | net.read | no | api.nasdaq.com | US rows only; day offset calibrated by the merge skill |
| `earnings_calendar(day)` | net.read | no | api.nasdaq.com | market-cap floor (200 B USD) |
| `rss_headlines(feed)` | net.read | no | CNBC, MarketWatch | named feeds only; https links only |
| `index_quote(symbol)` | net.read | no | Yahoo chart API (query1 → query2) | `^SYMBOL` pattern; 429-aware |
| `llm_json(system, user)` | llm.call | no (uses plan quota) | Qwen Token Plan, OpenAI-compatible (`qwen3.7-plus`) | mission budget: calls, tokens, USD; key from Secrets Manager `market/prod` in k8s, env or `E:\repos\.ENV` locally |
| `daily_history(symbol, range)` | net.read | no | Yahoo chart API | `^INDEX` only; 1y/2y/5y |
| `intraday(symbol, range, prepost)` | net.read | no | Yahoo chart API, 5-minute bars | `ES=F`/`NQ=F`/`YM=F` or a stock ticker from the earnings calendar; 1d/5d/60d |
| `publish_file(name, doc)` | fs.publish | **yes** | local volume | name pattern; atomic rename; idempotency key; publish lock |

Every call checks the contract's permissions and the host allowlist **before** a socket opens, and is
recorded in `usage` (latency, tokens, cost, success).

## 5. Skills (deterministic know-how, `skills.py`)

| Skill | Used by | What it knows |
|---|---|---|
| release taxonomy `classify_release` | data | which US releases matter, their family, category, tier, rate sensitivity |
| `calibrate_day_offset` | data | infers a calendar source's day shift from weekly claims always landing on Thursday |
| Eastern time `et_offset`, `fixed_offset_to_et` | data | US DST without tzdata; Nasdaq prints times at a fixed UTC-4 |
| `normalize_macro` / `normalize_fomc` / `normalize_earnings` | data, researcher | rows → events; the FOMC from both sources dedupes to one id |
| `dedupe_rank` | data | keeps the window's tier-1/2 events first, caps the count |
| `index_sensitivity` | analyst, critic, aggregator | 0–3 exposure of each index to an event (Dow membership, Nasdaq heavyweights, market cap) |
| `predict_event` — the baseline predictor | analyst fallback, analyst input | drift, momentum, consensus-implied change, surprise vs consensus once released, expected earnings change, beat base rate; probability capped at 66 % before a release, 80 % after |
| `day_outlook` | data | combines a day's event calls, weighted by exposure, sub-linear in the count |
| `fit_logistic`, `backtest_gap` | data | P(up close \| open gap) fitted by Newton's method; out-of-sample test against the always-up baseline |
| `futures_move`, `futures_check` | data | the overnight futures move (prior 4 PM ET bar → latest bar), and the same reading backtested at 9:20 ET |
| `after_hours_move`, `implied_index_move` | data | a reporter's after-hours move, translated into each index (cap weight, or price ÷ Dow divisor) |
| `combine`, `gap_probability` | data | market evidence added in log-odds to the event view (events at half weight) |
| `score_calls` | data | hit rate and Brier score per index against realised closes |
| `rules_impact` | analyst fallback | bilingual summary, scenarios and what to watch |
| `advice_language`, `unsupported_numbers` | critic, verifier | refuses advice wording; flags numbers whose value (allowing sign, rounding and K/M/万/亿 units) appears nowhere in the inputs |

## 6. The task graph

```
collect.fomc ─┐
collect.macro.<day> ×14 ─┼─(soft)─▶ merge ─▶ verify.events ─▶ analyze.b0 ─▶ critic.b0 ─┐
collect.earnings.<day> ×10 ┘                                 analyze.b1 ─▶ critic.b1 ─┤   (critic rejects?)
collect.snapshot ─(soft, context for analyst/critic/assemble)    …                    ├─▶ analyze.b1.r1 ─▶ critic.b1.r1 ─┐
collect.headlines ─(soft)                                                             └──────────────────────────────────┴▶ assemble ─▶ verify.timeline ─▶ publish
```

* **Hard deps** must succeed; **soft deps** only need to finish — a dead source is skipped, not fatal.
* The analysis layer does not exist at plan time: the coordinator adds it when `merge` reports how many events there are (dynamic fan-out), and adds revisions when the critic rejects. Every addition is checked for cycles and budget.
* Task states: `pending → ready → leased → succeeded`; `leased → ready` (retry with backoff 2ⁿ s) `→ dead`; `ready → awaiting_approval → ready`; `pending → skipped` when a hard dependency died.

## 7. Durable state (PostgreSQL in k8s, SQLite locally — same SQL)

| Table | Holds |
|---|---|
| `missions` | goal, intent, params, status, deadline, idempotency key, outcome report |
| `tasks` | the DAG: role, deps, inputs, status, attempts, lease owner/expiry, backoff, output artifact, approval |
| `events` | the append-only message log agents communicate through, and the execution timeline |
| `artifacts` | immutable, content-addressed outputs (`role.op:<sha256>`) |
| `checkpoints` | per-task working memory (quotes fetched so far, the model's answer before commit) |
| `side_effects` | idempotency records: one publish per mission × content |
| `locks` | leases on shared resources (`publish:market-timeline`) |
| `escalations` | what needs a human, why, how it was resolved |
| `timers` | scheduled and event-driven wake-ups; the timer id is the mission's idempotency key |
| `knowledge` | long-term memory by namespace: `analysis_cache` (12 h), `outlook_log` (calls frozen at 9:30 ET, with the futures that informed them), `calibration` (the verified signal), `source_health`, `eval_cases`, `published` (incl. the last full timeline, for the pre-open update), `risks`, `hooked` |
| `usage` | every tool and model call: latency, tokens, cost, success |

Memory layers: **mission state** (missions/tasks) · **working memory** (checkpoints) · **episodic history**
(events) · **shared knowledge** (knowledge) · **reusable skills** (skills.py) · **artifacts** (artifacts, timeline.json).

## 8. How each principle is met

| Principle | Where |
|---|---|
| Durable execution, resume after crash | every transition is a committed row; `Coordinator.step()` keeps no state between steps; test `test_coordinator_and_store_restart_mid_mission_resume_without_duplicates` |
| Idempotent tasks | `add_tasks` no-ops on existing keys; timers → missions by idempotency key; publish by `side_effect_once`; tests `test_timer_fired_twice…`, `test_publish_retry_writes_once` |
| Workers and queues | `Worker.run_one` leases inside one serialised write transaction (Postgres advisory lock / SQLite `BEGIN IMMEDIATE`); any number of workers / pods |
| Leases, ownership, no conflicts | lease + heartbeat; commits fenced by lease owner; publish lock; tests `test_stale_worker_cannot_overwrite…`, `test_concurrent_workers_never_claim_the_same_task` |
| Checkpoints | snapshot per symbol; analyst answer saved before commit; test `test_analyst_crash_after_model_answer_does_not_pay_twice` |
| Verification agents, critic loop | critic per batch + verifier on events and on the timeline; revision with feedback, then baseline fallback |
| Replanning | dynamic fan-out after merge; revisions after rejection; approval gate after risky verification |
| Local failure handling | retries with backoff per task; optional sources degrade; nothing restarts the mission |
| Escalation | dead required task, revision limit, majority of sources down, deadline, repeated probe failures |
| Autonomy control | permission per contract; host allowlist; publish behind verification and, when risky, a human |
| Limits on delegation | `max_tasks`, `max_depth`, `max_parallel`, `max_llm_calls`, `max_llm_tokens`, `max_cost_usd`, deadline, per-agent timeouts and tool-call caps |
| Observability, execution timeline | `explain`, `metrics`, `mission_report`; the page's "How this was made" panel |
| Scheduling / wake-ups | standing timers + post-release timers; `coordinator` loop fires them |
| Safety boundaries | permissions, allowlist, advice filter, number-provenance check, atomic writes, textContent-only rendering, separate namespace with egress only for workers |
| Multi-agent evaluations / disaster recovery | `tests/test_desk.py`: 27 cases covering coordination, killed workers, stale commits, double claims, store and coordinator restart, cascading source failure, deadlines, budget, critic loops, permission denials |
| System-level reliability | `metrics`: mission completion rate, task success rate, recovery rate, retries, human interventions, agent utilisation, cost and latency |
| Continuous improvement | critic rejections past the revision limit are kept as `eval_cases`; every call is scored (hit rate, Brier) and shown on the page |

## 9. Known limits

* The baseline predictor has a small edge at best. Equities rise on slightly more than half of sessions, so it leans "up" unless an event argues otherwise. The track record will show whether it, or the model, beats a coin flip; treat both as commentary.
* Market holidays are not modelled; a holiday shows as a session with a call and no score.
* Nasdaq's quirks (day shift, fixed UTC-4 times) are detected or encoded, and the verifier checks the claims-on-Thursday invariant; a further layout change fails loudly rather than silently.
* The database is PostgreSQL and reached over the network, but the published `timeline.json` sits on a node-local volume shared by the workers and `desk-web`; several nodes need an RWX volume or serving the file from the database.
